claims.text: Ti40Ni40Cr10Al5V5 is presented as a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy satisfying the stated compositional criteria.
Adding 0.5–2 wt% yttrium oxide precursor, with about 1 wt% preferred, is the proposed intervention.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering at 1100–1200 °C under a reducing atmosphere will facilitate in-situ formation of Y2O3 dispersoids.
The reducing atmosphere will prevent unwanted oxidation.
The intervention will produce a homogeneous, uniform dispersion of nanoscale Y2O3 particles in the alloy matrix.
The Y2O3 dispersoids will be thermally stable at elevated temperature.
Y2O3 dispersoids will impede dislocation motion.
Y2O3 dispersoids will restrict grain-boundary sliding and pin microstructural features.
Impeded dislocation motion and restricted grain-boundary sliding will increase elevated-temperature yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion and restricted grain-boundary sliding will improve elevated-temperature creep resistance.
The oxide-containing alloy will have significantly higher high-temperature yield strength than the identically processed oxide-free alloy.
The oxide-containing alloy will have better creep resistance than the identically processed oxide-free alloy.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on the uniformity and stability of the dispersoids.
The strengthening effect is anticipated at temperatures above approximately 600 °C.
Keeping the oxide addition between 0.5 and 2 wt% will maintain the HEA composition and avoid deleterious effects.

contradictions.description: The example Ti40Ni40Cr10Al5V5 is described as meeting the stipulated HEA composition criteria, but Ti and Ni are each 40 at%, exceeding the query's stated upper bound of 35 at% per element.
